clue.text: Warrior queen loses two articles — one of clothing

indicators.note: the queen's name gives up letters, so the named pieces are taken out of it

parts.note: Boadicea was the queen of the Iceni who fought the Romans in Britain
A is the indefinite article, so two articles are two As

explanation.surface: A fighting queen strips off a couple of garments, leaving just one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of clothing' reads as 'one article of clothing', the article echoing the two articles lost: take both As out of BOADICEA, Britain's rebel queen also called Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is a close-fitting upper garment, so it is one item of dress.

clue.text: Where shell-bursts get one in the soup ?

definitions.text: Where shell-bursts get one in the soup ?

parts.words: Where shell-bursts get one in the soup ?
parts.note: shell-bursts are hatchings, not explosions, and the home they happen in is an edible delicacy in Chinese soup

explanation.walkthrough: 'shell-bursts' and 'in the soup' (in trouble) suggest war; the shells are eggs hatching, and swiftlets' saliva homes are made into a Chinese soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs hatch in a bird's home, and the swiftlet's version is the base of a famous Chinese soup.

clue.text: Christian needed Help to overcome this Pessimism

definitions.text: Christian needed Help to overcome this

explanation.surface: A believer must be rescued from gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Christian falls into the Slough of Despond and a character named Help pulls him out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Slough named in Bunyan's allegory, and an old word for dejection or loss of hope.

clue.text: Literary professor as opposed to a juror

explanation.surface: An academic writer sits on the other side from the jury.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Challenger is Conan Doyle's explorer in The Lost World; a party in a trial may challenge, or object to, a juror.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's fictional scientist, and a person who objects to a member of the jury being seated.

clue.text: Man of many jobs including barbering in Seville ?

explanation.surface: A handyman whose trades extend to cutting hair in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Figaro, Rossini's Barber of Seville, sings 'Largo al factotum', calling himself the town's do-everything man.
explanation.definitionFit: A general servant who does every kind of work, and the title Figaro the barber gives himself in Rossini's opera.

clue.text: Like sea-rovers they are commonly dropped

parts.note: as means like
pirates rove the seas

explanation.surface: Like buccaneers, people who often get thrown overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The breathy H sound is an aspirate; dropping your aitches is thought of as common speech in Britain, so 'commonly' carries both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirates are H sounds, which careless speakers leave out.

clue.text: Organized teachers upset over a fish

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns a word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the NUT is Britain's National Union of Teachers, teachers organized into a union

explanation.surface: A teachers' union gets cross about a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NUT to TUN; 'over' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean food fish.

clue.text: Education gets it out in a different way

indicators.note: the letters are set out in another order, a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Schooling finds things out by another route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different way' rearranges IT OUT IN; the second 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, which is what education gives.

clue.text: Beth's family in Cambs …

explanation.surface: Where a girl's relatives live in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Beth is one of the March sisters in Little Women; March is a town in Cambridgeshire (Cambs), an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the sisters in Alcott's novel, and a fenland town in that county.

clue.text: . will be a little late this year

definitions.text: will be a little late this year

parts.words: will be a little late this year
parts.note: continues the previous clue: a month comes one day later than usual in a year with an extra day in February

explanation.walkthrough: The dots join it to 8 Down: March starts a day later when February gains its twenty-ninth day.
explanation.definitionFit: A year with an extra day added to February bears this name.

clue.text: Flushed perhaps but got up and took nourishment

parts.note: to rise is to get up; its past tense
to eat is to take nourishment; its past tense

explanation.surface: Someone rises red-faced from bed and has breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: rose-pink is one way of being flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rosy pink, the colour of a flushed cheek.

clue.text: Carried by Neddy, or on my lady's hip

explanation.surface: Something borne either by a donkey or worn at a woman's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neddy' is a British pet name for a donkey; the second sense is the old hooped frame that puffed a skirt out over the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket slung across a beast of burden, and also a framework extending a skirt at the hips.

clue.text: Killjoy ruins the wine

parts.note: to ruin something is to spoil it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A party pooper wrecks the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is a person who stops others' fun, just like a killjoy.

clue.text: Drinker from a kettle ?

parts.note: a heavy drinker is said to drink like this creature, and a long pan called a kettle is made for cooking it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone drinking straight from the teapot; the creature that 'drinks' is the one cooked in a fish kettle and proverbially drinks like one.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature living in water is a byword for heavy drinking and is poached in a long pan named a kettle after it.

clue.text: Performed like Ananias

explanation.surface: Acted the part of a liar from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts 5, Ananias lied about money, fell dead and was carried out by young men to be buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Performed means executed or done, and the Bible's Ananias was borne out of the room dead.

clue.text: But beginners at chess should study them too

definitions.text: But beginners at chess should study them too

parts.words: But beginners at chess should study them too
parts.note: plays the opposite of beginnings against beginners: the final phase of chess games is also worth studying

explanation.walkthrough: Novices usually study openings; the clue says they should also study the final stages of a game, where few pieces remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess endgames are the closing phases of games, a standard subject of study for players.

clue.text: Her box held hope for many

definitions.text: Her box held hope for many

parts.words: Her box held hope for many
parts.note: a prophetess left a sealed box said to contain secrets to save the world, to be opened only before bishops

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like Pandora, whose box kept hope; it is Joanna Southcott, the English prophetess whose sealed box followers believed would bring salvation.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna, the Devon prophetess, left the famous sealed box her followers awaited being opened.

clue.text: Educated in trade reorganization

indicators.note: a reorganization rearranges what is there, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone learned their skills through a shake-up of their industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganization' rearranges IN TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled or taught a skill has been educated.

clue.text: Tired out after record — result of bad reporting ?

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the record in the answer

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Exhausted after setting a record, the subject of a poor press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on 'Tired', and 'after' places the result behind the record. The question mark flags the definition as an example: bad press is one cause of lost reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unflattering press reports damage someone's reputation, bringing loss of good name.

clue.text: Still life scene

parts.note: not a painting of fruit but a motionless scene from life acted out by people holding a pose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still life' suggests a painting genre, but the scene is a living one held still, as in a tableau vivant.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people posed silently to represent a scene is a stage picture of that name.

clue.text: Traps a saucy wench

explanation.surface: Snares a cheeky young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' is not a verb but an old word for belongings or luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps are personal belongings or luggage, and an impudent girl is called this.

clue.text: Crazy Prussians dropping in — can you beat it ?

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters left are muddled into a new order
the word in falls out of the Prussians' letters before they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild Germans burst in unannounced: could anything top that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' scrambles PRUSSIANS and 'dropping' takes the letters of 'in' out of it, leaving PRUSSAS to rearrange. The definition is a challenge: to beat a record is to go beyond it.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to beat or outdo, the challenge behind the phrase.

clue.text: Propitiate with a soft sort of pudding

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
pease pudding is a British dish of boiled split peas

explanation.surface: Win someone over with a mushy dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To propitiate is to placate or calm an angry party.

clue.text: Mark the retreat of the North American soldiers

indicators.note: a retreat is a going back, so the following letters are read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Note how US troops pulled back from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the retreat of' turns NGIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or symbol, as in a plus sign.

clue.text: Ghost's beard was "a —— silvered" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Horatio describes the dead king's beard in Hamlet as black flecked with grey, and the missing heraldic word means black

explanation.walkthrough: Horatio says of the Ghost's beard 'It was, as I have seen it in his life, a sable silvered': sable is black in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black, filling Shakespeare's gap.

clue.text: His life's ruled by custom

parts.note: custom here means trade from customers, so this is a person whose livelihood depends on buyers

explanation.walkthrough: 'custom' looks like tradition but means patronage: customers coming to a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer running a store lives by the custom, or patronage, of buyers.

clue.text: No ruddy mug, when dealing with Red Indians

parts.note: not ruddy means without colour, wan
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A pasty complexion when meeting Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: In Westerns, white people are called this by Native Americans; the definition is that context, the dated term 'Red Indians' giving the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Western films give white settlers in the mouths of Native Americans.

clue.text: Cambridge Park, E 11 01-989
A bold front starts with an aid to one

definitions.text: A bold front starts with an aid to one

parts.words: A bold front starts with an aid to one
parts.note: a show of boldness is a bold front, and the word begins with the undergarment that supports a woman's front

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'A bold front'; the rest says the word starts with BRA, an aid to a front in the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering display of courage, a bold front put on to impress.

clue.text: Mystery writer turns into fat beast

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: the writer's name turns round and is read backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote early detective and mystery stories

explanation.surface: A crime novelist gets heavier and becomes a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the writer's name, and 'into' sets it inside the fat; 'beast' at the end is the definition, not 'fat beast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard is a big spotted cat, a wild animal.

clue.text: The last man in the vineyard at this hour

definitions.text: The last man in the vineyard at this hour

parts.words: The last man in the vineyard at this hour
parts.note: in the parable of the labourers in Matthew's Gospel the last workers are hired late in the day yet paid a full wage

explanation.walkthrough: The parable's latecomers were hired at the hour that has given us the phrase for something done at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible parable the final labourers start work at this late hour of the day.

clue.text: Bear witness at a trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Give evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to testify or certify that something is true.
